title: Purification of murine cortex mitochondria using a modified magnetic bead isolation method☆
author: Josic, Ujevic, et al.
materials: As seen in Fig. 1, Method 1 consistently yields highly pure mitochondria in respect to the plasma membrane, with no PMCA isoforms detected across all repetitions. Method 3, based on a simple differential centrifugation method reported by Mukherjee et al. [3] and the Miltenyi Biotec Mitochondria Isolation kit, showed the lowest reproducibility, with PMCA still being highly abundant in most final fractions of isolated mitochondria. Method 2, also based on the commercial Miltenyi kit protocols as Method 1, showed higher reproducibility than Method 3 but still lower purity in comparison to Method 1. Furthermore, this method shows the lowest yield among the three methods, presumably due to the additional chromatography purification step. Method 1, being the simplest and yielding the highest mitochondrial purity, is the optimal of the three described methods.Fig. 1a) The purity of final isolated mitochondrial fractions compared by method, assessed by Western blotting against panPMCA, a plasma membrane marker, and TOM20, outer mitochondrial membrane marker. Presented are 6 isolations corresponding to 6 samples per method, with a total of 18 final purified mitochondrial fractions checked for purity a) low-femtogram sensitivity substrate was used for chemiluminescence visualization. b) Quantification of the final mitochondrial fraction purity using a ratio of panPMCA and TOM20 chemiluminescence intensity. Final protein yield was assessed using a BCA assay, with final concentrations: γ (m3) = 1014.36 µg/mL, γ (m4) = 808.64 µg/mL, γ (m5) = 88.36 µg/mL, γ (m6) = 41.82 µg/mL, γ (m7) = 730.36 µg/mL, γ (m8) = 341.18 µg/mL, γ (m9) = 73.09 µg/mL, γ (m10) = 73.18 µg/mL, γ (m11) = 184.55 µg/mL, γ (m12) = 70.91 µg/mL, γ (m13) = 329.18 µg/mL, γ (m14) = 1587.45 µg/mL, γ (m15) = 765.00 µg/mL, γ (m16) = 621.91 µg/mL, γ (m17) = 865.91 µg/mL, γ (m18) = 463.91 µg/mL. Samples m1 and m2 were below detection limit (20 µg/mL). Error bars shown the number of replicates ± SEM (standard error of mean).Fig 1 dummy alt text

steps.title: Prepare all buffers on ice
steps.instruction: Prepare all buffers fresh for each isolation and keep them on ice throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Make 1X Solution 2
steps.instruction: Add 1 volume of 10X Solution 2 (Miltenyi Mitochondria Extraction Kit – Tissue, Cat#130‑097‑340) to 9 volumes of ddH₂O. Use 5 mL per 50 mg tissue; add an extra 10 mL for each Protease Inhibitor tablet when preparing Protease Inhibition Buffer.

steps.title: Make Extraction Buffer
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL of Solution 1 (same kit) to 0.5 mL of freshly prepared 1X Solution 2. Use 500 µL per 50 mg tissue.

steps.title: Make 1X Separation Buffer
steps.instruction: Incubate 10X Separation Buffer (Miltenyi Mitochondria Isolation Kit mouse tissue, Cat#130‑096‑946) at 37 °C until crystals disappear, then dilute 1:9 with ddH₂O. Use 23 mL per 50 mg tissue.

steps.title: Weigh cortex tissue
steps.instruction: Weigh murine cortex tissue to obtain ~50 mg ± 5 mg per sample.

steps.title: Wash tissue with Solution 2
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL Solution 2 to the tissue in an Eppendorf tube, incubate on ice for 5 min, discard; repeat three times.

steps.title: Homogenise in Extraction Buffer
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL Extraction Buffer, then gently homogenise with a Potter‑Elvehjem pestle by pressing tissue against the tube wall and rotating the pestle for 3 strokes.

steps.title: Incubate homogenate on ice
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube for 30 min on ice.

steps.title: Centrifuge low‑speed
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 5 min at 300 g, 4 °C; discard the supernatant completely.

steps.title: Add Protease Inhibition Buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL cold Protease Inhibition Buffer to the pellet, resuspend slowly by pipetting, and transfer the suspension to a cold gentleMACS C‑tube. Wash the original Eppendorf tube with another 1 mL cold Protease Inhibition Buffer and add this wash to the C‑tube.

steps.title: GentleMACS homogenisation
steps.instruction: Run the gentleMACS Dissociator with program m_mito_tissue_01 on the C‑tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge homogenate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the C‑tube 10 min at 500 g, 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the supernatant, leaving ~200–300 µL above the loose pellet; collect this supernatant without aspirating the pellet.

steps.title: Dilute with Separation Buffer
steps.instruction: Add cooled 1X Separation Buffer to the collected supernatant to a final volume of 10 mL and mix well.

steps.title: Add Anti‑TOM22 beads
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL Anti‑TOM22 magnetic beads to the 10 mL diluted sample.

steps.title: Incubate with beads
steps.instruction: Incubate 1 h at 4 °C with continuous gentle vortexing (≤20 rpm on a tube rotator).

steps.title: Prepare LS column
steps.instruction: Place an LS column on a MidiMACS Separator on the MACS Multistand, rinse with 3 mL 1X Separation Buffer, and attach a 30 µm Pre‑Separation Filter.

steps.title: Load sample onto column
steps.instruction: Add the bead‑incubated sample to the column in three aliquots of 3.3 mL each, allowing each to flow through completely.

steps.title: Wash column and filter
steps.instruction: Wash the filter and column with 3 × 3 mL Separation Buffer, letting each wash flow through before adding the next.

steps.title: Elute mitochondria
steps.instruction: Discard the filter, remove the column, place it above an Eppendorf tube, add 1.5 mL Separation Buffer, and firmly press the plunger to elute the bound mitochondria.

steps.title: Pellet eluate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the eluate 2 min at 13 000 g, 4 °C; discard the supernatant completely.

steps.title: First PBS wash
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL sterile Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free PBS to the pellet without disrupting it, immediately remove the supernatant, and centrifuge if needed (repeat centrifugation at 13 000 g, 2 min, 4 °C if pellet was disturbed).

steps.title: Second PBS wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the PBS wash exactly as in the previous step.

steps.title: Resuspend final pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed mitochondrial pellet in 100 µL Storage Buffer.

steps.title: Alternative Method 2 – Myelin removal (replace steps 11‑13)
steps.instruction: After step 10 (centrifugation at 500 g), add Myelin Removal Buffer and 20 µL Myelin Removal Beads per 50 mg tissue (plus 180 µL Buffer). Mix gently, incubate 15 min at 4 °C, then wash with 10× the Buffer volume added. Centrifuge 15 min at 1000 g, 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 1000 µL Myelin Removal Buffer. Prepare a fresh LS column, rinse with 3 mL 1X Myelin Removal Buffer, load the sample directly onto the column, collect flow‑through, wash column with 2 × 1 mL Myelin Removal Buffer and collect this effluent together with the previous flow‑through. Add cooled 1X Separation Buffer to the pooled effluent to a final volume of 10 mL and continue with the standard bead incubation (step 13 of Method 1).

steps.title: Alternative Method 3 – Lysis before step 11
steps.instruction: Instead of the Extraction Buffer step, wash the 50 mg tissue with 0.5 mL Lysis Buffer and discard immediately. Incubate in 10 % (v/w) Lysis Buffer for 15 min at 4 °C, then homogenise with Potter‑Elvehjem pestle (10–15 strokes). Add 1/9 volume of 100X Lysis Buffer (≈50 µL for 50 mg tissue), centrifuge 5 min at 3100 g, 4 °C, and collect the pellet. Transfer supernatant to a new tube and centrifuge 5 min at 30 200 g, 4 °C to pellet mitochondria. Add cooled 1X Separation Buffer to this pellet to a final volume of 10 mL, mix, add 50 µL Anti‑TOM22 beads, and then follow the standard protocol from step 13 onward (bead incubation, column purification, washes, and final resuspension).
